author: Susan Price
title: Campaign to name and shame companies fuelling Indonesia’s wildfire crisis
content:
An escalating wildfire crisis in Indonesia since July has covered much of Southeast Asia in a protracted and hazardous smoke haze.

Greenpeace Malaysia and Himpunan Advocacy Rakyat Malaysia (HARAM) held a peaceful protest outside the Indonesian embassy in Malaysia’s capital, Kuala Lumpur, on September 4, in solidarity with all communities affected by the cross-border haze and the loss of wildlife, suffered most severely in Indonesia.

The protesters did not blame Indonesians for the crisis but, instead called for the corporate interests that are complicit in the crisis — including Malaysian companies — to be named and shamed.

"While corporate executives sit comfortably in their air-conditioned offices earning millions of dollars in profit, it is the common citizens, workers, students and even the children of Malaysia and Indonesia who are breathing in and dying from the haze. Schools are closing down, and our basic human right to breathe is being taken away from us. Clean air doesn’t have a passport, nor does environmental devastation. We stand firmly in solidarity with the communities in Indonesia who are affected by these fires,” HARAM chairman Brendon Gan said in a statement.

“Our action called on the government of Indonesia to formally disclose concession maps, hotspot and fire investigation data, and other evidence identifying Malaysian-linked companies associated with fires and haze in Indonesia,” Heng Kiah Chun, interim country representative of Greenpeace Malaysia told Green Left.

“Investigations by Greenpeace Indonesia linked Malaysian-owned palm oil companies to transboundary haze, through the largest burned areas, between 2015–18, on their subsidiary land in Indonesia”, he explained.

Indonesian authorities announced on August 31 they are investigating 19 companies holding concessions where fires have affected 11,047 hectares across seven provinces. They said that 42 companies have been identified as holding concessions with high wildfire potential, but the companies under investigation have not been publicly named.

“We also called for the Indonesian government to publicly name the Malaysian companies it has identified as being involved, so that Malaysian civil society, regulators and parliament can pursue accountability within Malaysia.

“We further called for Indonesia to share this evidence with the Malaysian government on an ongoing basis through existing ASEAN mechanisms or direct bilateral channels, rather than relying on public allegations and press statements alone.

“Ultimately, we are calling for reciprocal disclosure and enforcement between both governments. This will provide each country with the means to investigate and hold accountable companies within its own jurisdiction, based on evidence that is openly shared between Indonesia and Malaysia.

“Transparency and cooperation are essential to ensuring that those responsible can be properly identified and held accountable, while protecting communities and the environment from recurring transboundary haze.”

The vast majority of palm oil traders have continued with business as usual to supply some of the world’s largest consumer brands in the Global North, Chun said. So the Global North has a responsibility ensure that these supply chains “are in accordance with the No Deforestation, No Peat, and No Exploitation (NDPE) policy”.

Financial institutions, such as banks, should equally have strong safeguards to ensure that their investments do not go into financing deforestation, peatland destruction, land degradation or activities linked to forest and peatland fires, Chun added.

“There is also a regional dimension to this responsibility. For example, Malaysian palm oil companies themselves should show their commitments through full transparency and by upholding the NDPE policy.”

Meanwhile, the Malaysian government has taken a number of measures to respond to the immediate impacts, including intensifying air-quality monitoring, prohibiting open burning, conducting cloud-seeding operations, providing firefighting assistance to Indonesia and closing schools where necessary, Chun added.

It declared an emergency in Serian, Sarawak, when the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index exceeded 500 and Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has called for ASEAN to review its mechanisms for addressing transboundary haze and its impacts on public health.

“However, these measures largely address the symptoms of the haze rather than its root causes. Cloud seeding …

author: Chiara Miraglia
title: What you need to know about the EU’s new digital deportation regime
content:
On 17 June, the European Parliament approved the new deportation law (called the “Return” Regulation) which aims to track undocumented people down and deport them from the EU in large numbers. The Regulation boosts the surveillance powers and digital control of national authorities and will rely heavily on technologies and data collection in their enforcement. This blog outlines the various digital tools and processes included in the EU’s new digital deportation regime.

By Protect Not Surveil (guest author) · September 23, 2026

On 17 June, the European Parliament approved the new EU’s deportation law (officially called the “Return” Regulation). The Deportation Regulation aims to track undocumented people down and deport them from the EU in large numbers. The most appalling of all the features of this new deportation system is the possibility for Member States to deport a person to a country they have never been to and detain them there indefinitely. More than 200 organisations petitioned against the legislative proposal, denouncing the new rules for what they are: inhumane.

The Regulation also boosts the surveillance powers and digital control of national authorities. Deportations rely heavily on technologies and data collection in their enforcement. At every step of the process, digital tools are used: to arrest and identify undocumented people, to detain them and restrict their movements, as well as to enforce deportation decisions.

The use of technologies severely undermine the digital and fundamental rights of people affected by this new regime, from data protection to asylum, dignity and liberty. The Deportation Regulation shows how migration and border control continue to serve as technological testing grounds for the EU and its Member States. They progressively but steadily widen the regime of exception at the core of the European data protection legal framework, and by doing so, irremediably undermine everyone’s fundamental rights.

The new deportation regime creates “obligations” on people without a valid residence or travel permit “to leave and cooperate”. To “promote” deportations and facilitate their identification, national authorities are authorised to take investigative measures, such as conducting home raids and searching any other “relevant premises” such as community centres, workplaces, hospitals, etc., force the collection of biometric data and search and seize personal belongings, electronic devices and “other items of relevance” – in other words literally anything from anyone. Further investigative measures defined under national law can also be deployed, which gives Member States a wide margin of discretion to introduce far-reaching ones.

Such practices codify the criminalisation of migrants and are disproportionate for migration management purposes. First, police raids without the requirement of independent judicial control in all EU countries will tarnish all places considered safe today and instill fear and insecurity among migrant communities and those providing services and support to them.

Second, coercion to collect biometric data, allegedly “as a last resort”, constitutes a grave infringement on the fundamental rights to dignity, integrity, liberty and security as it incentives the use of violence, punishment and detention. A 2018 report by Médecins du Monde showcased recurrent degrading treatments by Belgian police forces, sometimes amounting to torture (confinement in underwear in “freezer-cells”, blackmail, physical violence, etc.), against migrants in response to their refusal to give their fingerprints. The new provision allowing coercion is nothing less than a laissez-passer for further physical and psychological abuses.

Third, the search and seizure of electronic devices is extremely intrusive and manifestly disproportionate. Phone data extraction in particular can lead to the wide collection of sensitive data including data that is not necessarily relevant to the administrative procedure. In Germany, the Federal Administrative Court declared the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees’ (BAMF Migration Office) routine practice of searching asylum seekers’ mobile phones without cause unlawful. Seizing devices also encourages the procurement and use of hacking tools to bypass their security systems (pass-codes, PIN numbers, etc.), like Israeli company Cellebrite’s UFED (Universal Forensics Extraction Device), which can extract data even from locked smartphones in certain …

author: Unknown
title: Leonardo Caffo - Rethinking Lampedusa
content:
Author

: Leonardo Caffo

Title

: Rethinking Lampedusa

Subtitle

: Conceptual Architecture and the Philosophy of Europe’s Paradox

Date

: 2026

Source

: Anthropology (journal of) 2026


Abstract


 Lampedusa is habitually narrated as a site of emergency, yet its condition is structural rather than exceptional. This paper argues that the island functions as a paradox-object through which Europe’s constitutive contradictions become legible: geographically African, juridically European, and symbolically the very membrane that renders the two categories thinkable as distinct. Drawing on Foucault’s dispositif, Deleuze’s typology of continental and oceanic islands, and Achille Varzi’s distinction between fiat and bona fide boundaries, the paper shows that Lampedusa’s administrative and political borders systematically fail to coincide with its own geology — a mismatch condensed in the island’s municipal pairing with the volcanic, geologically European Linosa. Reading Agamben’s homo sacer against Hardt and Negri’s new barbarians, the paper treats the migrant not as a single, settled figure but as the site of two irreconcilable theoretical wagers, staged empirically in the recurring legal confrontation between Italian anti-NGO decrees and search-and-rescue obligations under international maritime law. Building on original fieldwork from the Rethinking Lampedusa research residency (2022–2025), the paper proposes reading the island as an anarchic object — a site where sovereignty is permanently held in default — and extends this default beyond the human register via Rosi Braidotti’s critical posthumanism, arguing that the same arche which excludes the migrant also subtends the human/non-human hierarchy visible in the island’s shared ecology of turtle nesting sites and disembarkation quays. The paper closes by proposing, through Rancière’s partage du sensible and Ariella Azoulay’s civil contract of photography, a counter-design for Lampedusa’s spatial and visual regime — one that would force the coexistence, rather than the segregation, of the island’s tourist and migrant economies. This remains, deliberately, an open rather than a concluding argument: further sections will need to test the proposal against concrete institutional and architectural alternatives.


 Keywords: Lampedusa; Linosa; new barbarians; fiat boundaries; Mediterranean migration; search and rescue; European Union border regime


Methodological Note: Practice-Based Research and the Position of the Author


 This paper departs, at several points, from the conventions of purely textual philosophical argument by drawing on material generated through Rethinking Lampedusa, a research and art-residency program the author has coordinated since 2022. It is necessary to state explicitly what kind of evidentiary status this material is being given, since practice-based research operates under different epistemic warrants than either empirical social science or textual exegesis, and conflating the three would misrepresent what is being claimed. The fieldwork referenced in Section 1.1 and elsewhere does not constitute ethnographic data in the disciplinary sense: it was not collected under a formal research protocol, does not involve systematic interviewing, coding, or triangulation, and makes no claim to generalizability beyond the specific, repeated, situated encounters it records. What it offers instead is what practice-based research literature has termed embodied and situated knowledge — insight generated through sustained, reflexive presence in a site, mediated by artistic and pedagogical practice (the residency’s Moleskine notebooks, workshops, and exhibitions) rather than by observation held at methodological arm’s length. This is a recognized, if still contested, mode of knowledge production within philosophy of art, aesthetics, and increasingly within border and migration studies, where scholars such as Federica Mazzara (cited throughout this paper) have similarly drawn on direct engagement with artistic and activist practice on Lampedusa itself to ground theoretical claims that pure textual analysis could not have generated independently.


 Three consequences follow from this status, and the reader should hold them in mind throughout.


 First, the fieldwork material functions in this paper as illustrative and generative, not as evidentiary in the sense a claim like “in April 2026, nineteen migrants died of hypothermia” is evidentiary, where the latter is …

author: Unknown
title: HPG announces the death of German internationalist Pablo Manuel Figueiras Duarte
content:
The People’s Defence Forces (HPG) announced the death of guerrilla fighter Pablo Manuel Figueiras Duarte. The internationalist, who was known within the Kurdish freedom movement as Baran Nûjiyan Salîma, was born in Germany to a German mother and a Portuguese father. According to the HPG, he joined the guerrilla ranks in 2019 and was active in areas including Gare, Metîna and Qandil. He lost his life in Qandil on August 6, 2025.


The ID information of the fallen internationalist guerrilla fighter is as follows:


Nom de Guerre: Baran Nûjiyan Salîma


First-Last Name: Pablo Manuel Figueiras Duarte


Birthplace: Germany


Mother's-Father's Name: Angela – Romeu


Date and Place of Death: 6 August 2025 – Qandil


The obituary published by the HPG Press Centre reads as follows:


“Our comrade Baran Nûjiyan was born in Germany into an internationalist family, to a Portuguese father and a German mother. Although he grew up in a family environment where different cultures came together, from a very young age he began to fundamentally question the structure of capitalist modernity, which turns human beings into objects, strips them of their spirit and alienates them from their own essence.


With great seriousness, our comrade devoted himself to his education and successfully completed his university studies. Afterwards, he worked in various fields and earned his own living. The experiences he gained under the difficult conditions of working life sharpened his understanding of the reality of the capitalist system, the exploitation of human labor, and the social relations that increasingly isolate the individual.


Baran recognized that, within this capitalist predicament that constrains both mind and spirit, human beings cannot remain true to their human essence, their ethical principles, and their pursuit of freedom. For this reason, from a young age he began searching for a radical alternative way of life.


In the heart of Europe, he established close ties with various political circles, groups, and movements that regarded themselves as opponents of the capitalist system, seeking answers to his existential questions among them. However, when he realized that these oppositional structures were far from producing a genuine revolutionary alternative, he continued his search without interruption.


In 2018, he became acquainted with the Kurdish Freedom Movement, in which he saw the most radical and genuine response to humanity’s universal quest for freedom. The more deeply he engaged with the ideological, psychological, and sociological analyses of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] and the paradigm of a women’s liberationist, ecological, and democratic society, the more strongly he felt that he had found the historical truth he had been searching for.


But Baran was not influenced by theoretical texts alone. The attitude, consistency in life, and determination of the Apoist militants he met in Europe also left a profound impression on him. Unlike other circles critical of the system, the Apoists lived according to their convictions, put the principles they advocated into practice in every moment of their lives, and were prepared to make the greatest sacrifices for the values of freedom they defended. For him, this attitude fundamentally distinguished them from all other groups.


In light of this, he immersed himself ever more deeply in the study of Leader Apo and the Kurdish Freedom Movement. The more he studied, understood, and drew closer to what he regarded as the truth, the more firmly he embraced the Apoist philosophy. Having attained a radical clarity intellectually, spiritually, and ethically, Comrade Baran became convinced that no idea could change the world as long as it remained purely theoretical.


Like the Apoists he had come to know, he believed that he too had to shoulder the full historical burden of the revolution. With this determination, he left behind all the individual opportunities offered by capitalist Europe, an academic career, and a life within the system, and turned toward the free and powerful mountains of Kurdistan.


In 2019, our comrade Baran committed his entire life to joining the guerrilla. He completed his initial guerrilla and militant training in Gare, one of the striking regions of the Medya Defense Zones. He began his revolutionary journey with a clear ideological consciousness.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Poll: Approval of Socialism at Record High as Capitalist Principles Hit New Lows
content:
Views of big business and free enterprise have declined significantly in the past decade.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

New polling finds that Americans approve of socialism more than ever, surpassing the 40 percent threshold for the first time in a Gallup survey as left-wing ideas and politicians surge in popularity.

According to Gallup polling conducted last month, 43 percent of Americans say they have a positive view of socialism. In Gallup’s 16 years of polling this question, the proportion of Americans saying as such has never before surpassed 40 percent. This is a four-point increase from 2025, when 39 percent said they had a positive view of the ideology — a slight increase from 36 percent in 2010.

Socialism is most popular among young people, with 57 percent of those aged 18 to 34 saying they view it positively.

Democrats’ view of socialism has steadily become more popular since 2010 — with those viewing it positively rising from 50 percent in 2010 to 65 percent in 2019 — and has stayed steady since then.

The big change in the past year, rather, has been driven by independents; in 2025, 37 percent of independents said they had a favorable view of socialism, lower than the average. That proportion rose by 8 points in the past year to 45 percent — now higher than the average among all Americans.

The polling comes as socialist figures like New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani have surged in popularity, with Mamdani enjoying strong approval ratings among New Yorkers and in national surveys. It adds to a slate of other polls showing surging popularity for the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) and the democratic socialist ideology, with Quinnipiac finding recently that over a quarter of voters in the U.S. now consider themselves supporters of DSA.

The surge in popularity comes even as the Trump administration is waging a fierce campaign to suppress left-wing groups and progressive ideology through its National Security Presidential Memorandum-7 (NSPM-7) initiative, which broadly equates principles like “anti-Americanism” and “anti-capitalism” with “criminal” speech.

But the capitalist principles that have long dominated the U.S. political system are also dropping in popularity, Gallup found.

According to the latest poll, only 35 percent of Americans have a positive view of big business, down from a high of 58 percent in 2012. Those who favor “free enterprise,” or the idea that businesses should operate relatively free from government regulation, have dropped from a proportion of nearly 90 percent to 77 percent in this year’s polling.

Approval of capitalism has also declined slightly from historic highs. For much of the 2010s, roughly 60 percent of Americans said they view capitalism positively. But that has since declined to roughly 55 percent.

While the changes to these opinions have largely been driven by Democrats, Gallup notes that the latest uptick in socialism’s approval “comes entirely from political independents.” Among Democrats, only 65 percent say they approve of free enterprise — down from 88 percent in 2021. Meanwhile, opinions of big business have cratered entirely among Democrats, from 48 percent in 2016 to a mere 17 percent in the latest poll.

content:
ΒΑΒ2026 ΣΚΟΠΙΑ – Ανταπόκριση


1η μέρα του 18ου Βαλκανικού Φεστιβάλ Βιβλίου, που διεξάγεται από την Πέμπτη 24 έως την Κυριακή 27/9 στην πρωτεύουσα της Βόρειας Μακεδονίας. Το infolibre είναι παρόν με τρία μέλη του και θα μεταδώσει τα των εκδηλώσεών του, που υπερβαίνουν τις τριάντα σε ένα εύρος πεδίων.


Όπως σημειώνουν οι διοργανωτές ο στόχος τους είναι να δημιουργηθεί ένας χώρος συλλογικά για συζητήσεις βασισμένες στους αγώνες, τις εμπειρίες και την οργάνωσή τους. Οι εκδηλώσεις θα επικεντρωθούν σε πεδία κρίσιμα για συλλογική αντίδραση, ανάλυση, και δράση στα σημερινά Βαλκάνια. Επιδιώκεται να συνεισφέρουν σε συγκεκριμένες και βασισμένες σε εμπειρίες στη βάση πρακτικές αντίστασης, φροντίδας, αλληλεγγύης. Πέρα από το σε τι είμαστε αντίθετοι, να εμβαθύνουμε στην πράξη στο τι μπορούμε να οικοδομήσουμε και μέσω αυτού να ενισχύσουμε τις σχέσεις μας με συντρόφους, πρωτοβουλίες, ομάδες.


Η κύρια εκδήλωση της πρώτης μέρας ήταν αφιερωμένη στη μνήμη του Nikola

Shteriov, εκ των βασικών συντελεστών της όλης πρωτοβουλίας, της Αναρχικής Συλλογικότητας Smovka και του κινήματος στα Σκόπια, που έφυγε πριν λίγο καιρό από τη ζωή τόσο νέος. Αρχικά προβλήθηκε ένα βίντεο με τις αγωνιστικές και συντροφικές σχέσεις του, ενώ στη συνέχεια μίλησαν σύντροφοι που τον γνώριζαν, μεταξύ των οποίων και από Clandestina Θεσσαλονίκης. Κύριο σύνθημα: FOR ALL OF US TO LIVE, AND NO ONE OF US TO RULE (Nikola Shteriov).


Επίσης, πραγματοποιήθηκε εκδήλωση για την τεχνολογία στην καθημερινή ζωή, όπου αναλύθηκαν τα εργαλεία της ΑΙ που χρησιμοποιούν οι καπιταλιστές, αλλά διατυπώθηκε και η αναγκαιότητα να πετύχουμε την ψηφιακή αυτονομία. Ενώ στη συζήτηση για την ψυχική και φυσική υγεία στον καπιταλισμό, παρουσιάστηκαν περιπτώσεις του τι βιώνει ο άνθρωπος και η κοινωνία μέσα σε συγκρούσεις, πολεμικές καταστάσεις, εγκλήματα πολέμου, αλλά και φοβίες στην καθημερινή ζωή όπως ισλαμοφοβία κα.

title: La trashumancia, forma de vida y producción milenaria
content:
Por Oscar Soto

*


La ganadería pastoril es una modalidad ancestral por la cual se cría el ganado haciendo uso de entornos variables a partir del desplazamiento de los animales y la gestión de las pasturas que lo abastecen. Esta dinámica de trabajo rural provee de medios a los campesinos que recorren pastizales alrededor del globo. Por eso, las familias se mueven en busca del recurso, y eso es bastante común, dado que las características de los espacios rurales de matorrales y estepas donde prospera el pastoreo son diversas. Las lluvias y nevadas estacionales son parte del sostenimiento de esas praderas infinitas. Podríamos decir que el pastoreo se vale de saberes tradicionales para sortear esos climas y ambientes sumamente hostiles donde la humedad y la altura son las únicas que pueden garantizar comida a las crías.


Unos 200 millones de personas en cerca de 100 países están abocados a esta labor. Es más, los pastores tradicionales, migratorios y transfronterizos en todo el planeta conservan los territorios de pastoreo y los utilizan para obtener carne, leche y otros alimentos, así como fibra, combustible y otros bienes. De hecho, el rol ecológico y social de esta práctica campesina e indígena es una de las razones que alientan la necesidad de su preservación. 


En términos generales, la cría de ganado es variable. Es posible definir, grosso modo

,

 una producción ganadera intensiva en la que los animales se concentran en un espacio determinado, alimentados por forrajes y suplementos determinados, la mayoría de las veces «importados» y con cierto automatismo. En tanto, en otro extremo, podemos identificar el pastoreo que proyecta en la labor humana un dispositivo central para su existencia, en espacios abiertos y naturales. 


Sobre este último, cabe mencionar lógicas distintas respecto de la propiedad y el acceso a la tierra, siendo los derechos privados exclusivos sobre la tierra, en general, menos comunes en las sociedades pastoriles. Es importante desanclar la idea de museo que objetiviza al mundo pastoril. Se puede ser pastor viviendo en un pueblo o en un paraje limítrofe con la ciudad. Sin embargo, lo cierto es que las características centrales del pastoreo apuntan a un modo de vida con lógicas y consecuencias diferentes a las de la ganadería intensiva.


Entre el conjunto de elementos que dan relieve a una práctica como esta se pueden mencionar cuatro aspectos centrales: la movilidad, que remite a la estacionalidad de la práctica haciendo del movimiento una forma más efectiva de adaptación y subsistencia; la territorialidad de pastizales: una gran porción de la superficie terrestre del planeta son pastizales, donde los medios de vida no pastoriles y la producción de alimentos suelen ser poco probables; la alta densidad nutricional de los alimentos que produce la actividad pastoril y la mejora de la biodiversidad que proporcionan. En su gran mayoría, los sistemas pastoriles emulan formas de vida silvestre reduciendo emisiones totales de gases de efecto invernadero y favoreciendo la producción baja en carbono.


El pastoralismo latinoamericano en zonas áridas es una actividad de larga data. En Argentina, pese a ser marginal, los animales suben a valles altos de unos 1.200 metros sobre el nivel del mar, en el caso de la Patagonia y el sur cuyano. La veranada –dirán los puesteros malargüinos–

es una forma de vida

 que los antecede en el sur de Mendoza, y es también una modalidad actual de puja por el territorio: la instrumentación de algunas leyes a mediados de los años 90 del siglo XX, tal el caso de la

Ley 6086 de Promoción y Arraigo de Puesteros en Zonas no Irrigadas

, no ha impedido la multiplicación de desalojos, lastimosamente vigentes en la actualidad.


En nuestro país, los sistemas de pastoreo extensivos han sido estrategias por las cuales el ganado se ha asemejado a un producto de riqueza social y cultural. De hecho, esta actividad involucra a más de 30.000 familias con distintos tipos de ganado, es decir, no solo chivos sino también vacunos, camélidos, ovinos, que se movilizan para obtener agua y pasturas, actividad que, además de cultural es económico-productiva. Para eso, es oportuno resaltar que —en lo relativo a los insumos que generan— solo el cálculo de ingresos del sector equivale a generar una riqueza de 300 millones de dólares cada año para el país, si miramos años regulares en términos económicos, sin tener en cuenta la megadevaluación de la moneda de principios de 2024.

1. Anarchy, acracy and the rule of the archons


by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article 

here


Because the term “anarchy” is so often used pejoratively to mean chaos, and because some contemporary anarchists are 

far from freedom-loving

, [1] people often look for a less off-putting term to describe the future society they would like to see.


I personally took to using “

real anarchism

” [2] to mark my own position, while others call themselves “voluntaryists” and here in France “

libertaires

“.


One term that is sometimes used to replace “anarchy” is “acracy”, although I suspect the label “acracist” is a non-starter for obvious reasons!


“Anarchy” 

means

 the absence of any “archy”, any form of government or rule, such as monarchy or oligarchy, [3] while “acracy” 

means

 the absence of any “cracy”, which is to say any coercive authority, such as plutocracy or so-called democracy. [4]


The term 

acracia

 first appeared in the Iberian world and is 

believed

 to have been invented by the Catalan syndicalist Rafael Farga i Pellicer (1844-1890), who founded a journal with that name. [5]


It was used by the likes of 

Peter Kropotkin

 (1842-1921) [6] and 

Martin Buber

 (1878-1965) [7] as a synonym for anarchy, but is seen by some as conveying the idea of a society that is 

ordered

, albeit in a voluntary and consensual manner, and/or as one without any kind of 

exploitation

 rather than without any kind of 

authority

, as is the case with anarchy. [8]


In a 2018 

interview

, French economist and thinker Frédéric Lordon argued that, etymologically, anarchy means the absence of an absolute foundation (

ᾰ̓ρχή, ărkhḗ

) on which power’s commandments can be based.


He said that because its political meaning is, in fact, a society in which there is neither power nor domination, the word should really be replaced by acracy, which is precisely that absence of power and domination (

κρατία, kratía

). [9]


With due respect to Lordon, the question does not seem to be as clear as he suggests. While the root word 

krátos

 can indeed 

mean

 “power, might”, [10] it can also mean an “act of strength, act of valour”, with the postulated Proto-Indo-European stem 

kret

 

also

 indicating “intelligence”. [11]


So acracy could alternatively be interpreted as a society without strength, valour and intelligence.


I think we may already be there!


Meanwhile, the 

ărkhḗ

 opposed by anarchy can be 

traced back

 to the verb 

ắrkhō

 which means, in the transitive sense, “to lead; to rule; to govern; to command” and, in the intransitive sense, “to be ruler; to hold an archonship”. [12]


My ears pricked up at that last word!


Historically, an archon 

was

 a chief magistrate of ancient Athens and more generally “a person who claims the right to rule, or to exercise power or sovereign authority over other human beings” or simply “a ruler, head of state or other leader”. [13]


But in the gnostic tradition it identifies “a supernatural ruler of the cosmos”. William Thompson has 

described

 “the cry of the archon Ialdabaoth that he was the Lord of the Universe and that there was nothing beyond him”. [14]


Per Shapiro writes about the archons in his book 

The War on Life: How We Are Manipulated by Archontic Intelligence

, which I 

reviewed

 in May this year. [15]


He explains that the archontic influence in our world is a psychopathic one which refuses to respect natural boundaries and human taboos: “In this range, we find everything from incest, rape and perversions to various manifestations of hubris, such as genetically manipulated crops, laboratory-made life and the fission of the atomic nucleus”. [16]


He sees this phenomenon as taking its most extreme form with Yahweh, the god of the Old Testament, who for the gnostics was a pretender god, “an insane demon who has the delusion of having created the universe. A deranged being who is jealous of the living planet and wants to destroy it”. [17]


There is definitely an anarchic flavour to the message from Sophia (Mother Earth) to archon leader Ialdabaoth: “The authority you claim rests on deception, and when the deception fails, you perish”. [18]

title: "Never Again": Czechoslovakian Hardcore in the Syrian Civil War
content:
In the following narrative, anarchists who participated as internationalist volunteers in the fight to defend Rojava against the Islamic State describe the role that the anti-militarist song “Už Nikdy” (“Never Again”) by the Czechoslovakian hardcore band Kritická Situace played in their experience.


This text is adapted from the newest issue of the anarchist hardcore publication

Inside Front

.

 We share it here to explore the importance of revolutionary music and culture in social movements.

The personal is geopolitical.


These events took place in March 2019, near the end of the fight against the Islamic State. At that time, the Turkish army and its Syrian proxies had brutally seized the majority-Kurdish district of Afrin in northwest Syria, and Donald Trump was

signaling

 that he would permit them to attack the rest of Rojava as well. At the same time, the Islamic State still controlled territory in Deir Ezzor in the southeast, where the final battles took place at al-Baghuz Fawqani.


As soon as the Islamic State was defeated, the United States government gave Turkey the green light to

butcher

 those who had defeated it. In 2024,

Turkish-backed forces

 came to power in Syria, creating

new challenges

 for the multiethnic revolutionary experiment in Rojava. Nonetheless, the fight for free life continues—in Rojava and the

rest

 of Syria, in

Turkey

, in Czech Republic and Slovakia, and even in the United States.

The struggle continues.


“Už Nikdy” by Kritická Situace.


We received the following accounts of the same events from two different correspondents.


Account I. — “Never Again”


In March 2019, I was in Syria, an internationalist volunteer in the midst of the civil war.


We were fighting on two fronts. To the northwest, our comrades were locked in a defensive war with Turkish proxies and the Turkish state itself, whereas we were engaged in an offensive war with Daesh in the southeast. To the northwest, death from above: snipers and drones. In the southeast, death from below: snipers and mines.


My friends and I were positioned on the second floor of an abandoned building in the ruins of the town of Al-Baghuz Fawqani. A Tweety Bird blanket was hung over one of the blacked-out windows in our room. There was a small kitten who would sleep with us. The comrades in the hospital to the north had sent us there with an ambulance. We took it forward to retrieve casualties from the front line, administering what care we could. Usually, I drove.


This cat briefly held the most advantageous position in the Syrian civil war.


In our group, there were volunteers from around the world who had come to Syria to defend the revolution. We found ourselves there in the last days of the last battle of the territorial war against the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria. In our ambulance unit, none of us shared common citizenship or a native tongue, but we soon found that we did share a background in the global punk counterculture.


One of the comrades described to me the sadness he had felt on the day that he had been forced to shave off his mohawk and flee his country. “But punk is not here,” he said, pointing at his hair. “It is here,” he said, pressing his fist to his heart.


“A Tweety Bird blanket was hung over one of the blacked-out windows in our room.”


By leaving my phone on the roof for several hours, I had managed to download a song titled “Never Again,” recorded in 1992 by the Czechoslovakian band

Kritická Situace

. The song had come to my attention in the year 1998, when it was featured in a memorable and impassioned review in

issue 11

 of the North American hardcore publication

Inside Front.

 It tells the story of a conscript fleeing from the army
through the wilderness, vowing that his superiors will never be able to force him to kill.


My friends and I were now in the exact inverse of that situation: we were internationalists who had crossed the world voluntarily to defend the principles of autonomy, ecology, and women’s liberation that the social movements in northeastern Syria were putting into practice. Still, war
is war. Many nights, after

tekmil

, we would sing “Never Again” together quietly in the darkness, to the sound of gunfire, mortar fire, and bombs. Those fluent in Slavic languages would sing the words, and the rest of us would carry the rhythms and harmonies as best we could.


In a dark dungeon, in the glow of torches,


You hide from the exercise of power.


You do not …

title: Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan'dan fon soruşturması açıklaması: Sorumluluğu olanlardan hesap sorulacak
content:
Cumhurbaşkanı Tayyip Erdoğan, kamuoyunda "fon krizi" olarak anılan ve 455 bin yatırımcıyı ilgilendiren soruşturmaya ilişkin, "Sermaye piyasalarının sınırlı bir alanında, belli sayıda fonda ortaya çıkan bir sorundan söz ediyoruz. Yani ne finansal sistemimize ne Türkiye ekonomisine yönelik bir risk söz konusu değil" dedi. Soruşturmanın sürdüğünü belirten Erdoğan, "Sorumluluğu olan kim varsa, bunlardan hukuk önünde hesap sorulacaktır” dedi.

Cumhurbaşkanı Tayyip Erdoğan, Birleşmiş Milletler BM 81. Genel Kurulu'na katılmak üzere gerçekleştirdiği New York ziyaretinin sonunda Türkevi'nde açıklamalarda bulundu ve gazetecilerin sorularını yanıtladı.

Erdoğan, 130'dan fazla ülkenin devlet ve hükümet başkanı düzeyinde temsil edildiği Genel Kurul etkinliklerinin bu yıl "Güveni Yeniden İnşa Etmek, Dönüşümü Yönetmek" temasıyla gerçekleştirildiğini söyledi.

BM Genel Kurulu'na hitap ettiğini hatırlatan Erdoğan, konuşmasında Türkiye'nin çok taraflılığa desteğini vurguladığını, bölgedeki gelişmelerle ilgili görüşlerini paylaştığını ve daha kapsayıcı, daha adil ve etkili bir küresel sisteme duyulan ihtiyacın altını çizdiğini söyledi. Erdoğan, Gazze'deki gelişmeleri de Birleşmiş Milletler kürsüsünden gündeme taşıdığını belirterek, "Gazzeli kardeşlerimize yönelik zulmü bir kez daha insanlığın gündemine taşıdık" dedi.

Erdoğan, Birleşmiş Milletler'in reforma ihtiyacı olduğu yönündeki görüşünün hatırlatılması ve nasıl bir Birleşmiş Milletler tasavvur ettiği sorusuna, “Mevcut yapı adil değil. Her şeyden önce bugün 190’dan fazla ülkenin iradesinin 5 ülkenin veto yetkisiyle sınırlandırıldığı bir Birleşmiş Milletler’den söz ediyoruz. Bu adaletsiz yapının, küresel istikrar ve huzuru koruyabilmesi, ortaya koyduğu temel ilkelere bağlı kalabilmesi, insanlığa vaadini yerine getirebilmesi mümkün değildir. Mesele yalnızca Türkiye'nin Birleşmiş Milletler'de daha fazla söz sahibi olması değil. Mesele Afrika’nın, Asya’nın, Latin Amerika’nın, İslam dünyasının, Avrupa’nın ve diğer bütün bölgelerin kendi tecrübeleriyle, kendi iradeleriyle bu küresel sistemde hakkaniyetli biçimde temsil edilme meselesidir. Bunun için diyoruz ki; veto mekanizması kaldırısın; sadece 5 üyeyi koruyan Birleşmiş Milletler modelinden, bütün üyeleri kuşatan bir mekanizmaya geçiş yapalım. Genel Kurul’u güçlü, kuvvetli ve etkin kılalım. Kurulacak yeni yapıda, seçilmiş üyelerin belirli sürelerle görev yaptığı, yeniden görev almak isteyenlerin uluslararası toplumun güvenini yeniden kazanmak zorunda olduğu, daha adil bir sistem olmalıdır” dedi.

Erdoğan, Filistin Devlet Başkanı Mahmud Abbas'ın iki yıl üst üste Birleşmiş Milletler'de bulunamamasını da uluslararası sistemdeki adaletsizliğin göstergelerinden biri olarak değerlendirdi. "Bizim meselemiz hiçbir ülkeye karşı olmak değildir. Bizim meselemiz adaletsizliğe karşı olmaktır" diyen Erdoğan, "Kendi adımıza mutluyuz ki o günlerden bu günlere hep tarihin doğru tarafında durduk, milletimizi utandıracak bir tek adım bile atmadık. Bugün dünya, bizim ilk gün söylediğimiz yere gelme eğilimindedir" ifadelerini kullandı.

Erdoğan, Hürmüz Boğazı'nda gemi trafiğinin azalmasına ilişkin soruya, gelişmelerin meselenin artık yalnızca İran ile ABD arasındaki bir sorun olmadığını gösterdiğini belirterek yanıt verdi. "Hürmüz Boğazı’nın gemi trafiğine kapatılmasına karşıyız. Hürmüz Boğazı’nda seyrüsefer serbestisinin korunması şarttır" diyen Erdoğan, bölgedeki her gerilimin Avrupa'yı, Asya'yı, enerji piyasalarını, taşımacılığı ve milyonlarca insanın günlük hayatını etkilediğini söyledi.

Erdoğan, Mekke Savunma Anlaşması'nın geleceğine ilişkin soruyu şöyle yanıtladı: "Mekke Savunma Anlaşması doğru yolda atılmış güçlü bir adımdır. Bu kadar zorlu bir coğrafyada böylesine önemli bir girişim yapıyorsanız bazı sınamalarla karşılaşmanız sürpriz değildir. Yeni bir şey söylerseniz, yeni bir irade ortaya koyarsanız, elbette bundan rahatsız olanlar çıkacaktır. Biz, dün kurulmuş bir devlet değiliz; tahriklere gelmeyecek, tuzağa düşmeyecek kadar tecrübeli bir devletiz.

Kurumsallaşma çalışmalarının tamamlanmasıyla yolumuzda daha güçlü ilerleyeceğimizden şüphem yok. Bölgenin sorunlarına bölge kaynaklı çözümler üretecek bir zeminin temelleri atılmıştır. Dışarıdan gelip bölgemize güvenlik reçetesi yazanların çoğu zaman geride daha fazla istikrarsızlık bıraktığını hep birlikte gördük. Diktiğimiz bu fidan, kısa sürede boy verecek ve bir çınara dönüşecektir. Biz ülkemize ve milletimize güveniyoruz, kardeşlerimize güveniyoruz.”

author: Fozzie
title: Direct Action (SolFed) #03 1997
content:
Issue 3 of Solidarity Federation's magazine.

Social Control: Political to Personal – An exploration of personal power, control, and responsibility from an anarcho-syndicalist perspective.

Science and Sexy Genes – Discussion on the search for genetic explanations for sexuality and the critique of scientific reductionism.

Roots of Elitism and Fascism – A brief history and critique of eugenics and its resurgence in modern policy.

Breaking the Laws of Language – Examination of language as a tool of social control and the politics of grammar and dialect.

IWA News Service – International updates on workers’ struggles, union actions, and direct action campaigns.

Direct Actions – Britain – Reports and opinions on direct actions and workplace struggles in the UK.

Anarchism: The FAQs – Fundamental questions and answers on racism, its roots, and strategies for resistance, with a focus on South Africa.

Closer Look: Social Democracy Reaches the Buffers – In-depth analysis of the state of railway unions, the failures of reformist unionism, and lessons for future organising.

Beanz Meanz Genes – Investigation into genetically engineered foods, industry practices, and consumer resistance.

Endpiece: Anarchy in Albania? – Reflections on recent uprisings in Albania, the nature of spontaneous revolt, and the need for organized alternatives.

title: GrapheneOS pas (que) pour les anarchistes ou pourquoi tout le monde devrait passer aux Google pixel
content:
Tu sais ce que c'est GrapheneOS ? Tu sais que tu peux l'installer facilement ? Vient on va voir comment on fait et pourquoi faut le faire :)


T'as perdu ton tél récemment ou il est en fin de vie et t'allais encore te racheter un Redmi ?


Attends deux secondes on t'explique un truc.


Si t'es anarchiste, sûrement tu sais déjà ce qu'est GrapheneOS (GOS) et pourquoi c'est utile de t'en procurer à la place de ton vieux bigot de toto.


Pour les autres par contre est ce que y aurait un intérêt à se procurer un tel téléphone ?


Les avantages :


• ça change quasi rien en terme d'utilisation par rapport à un smartphone classique


• plus il y aura du monde à avoir GOS et moins se sera suspect d'en avoir pour les gens qui en ont vraiment besoin, comme le fait d'utiliser TOR pour faire ses recherches par exemple


• tu peux facilement limiter les infos que tu donnes aux publicitaires (en plus de les limiter aussi pour les keufs)


Avertissement


On a pas envie de te pousser à utiliser encore plus de technologie et à te reposer encore plus sur les téléphones, mais si, comme la plupart des gens tu utilise un tél dans ta vie alors ça peut être bien de réfléchir à comment le faire au mieux.


Avant de voir comment faire, quelques rappel de ce qu'est GrapheneOs :


• GOS c'est un système d'exploitation

 comme Android ou IOS, c'est en gros ce qui fait marcher l'interface de ton smartphone et connecte les différents composants entre eux pour le faire fonctionner correctement


• GOS est fait pour la sécurité


il n'y a pas de traceurs publicitaire intégré, son mode de fonctionnement est connu et reconnu (pas comme IOS qui garde son fonctionnement opaque), il résiste à des tentatives d'intrusion publicitaire et des flics, etc. [1]


 /// MAINTENANT COMMENT FAIRE ? \\


1) TROUVER LE TÉL


• se procurer un téléphone Google Pixel


→ ça ne marche que sur ses téléphones pour le moment (le mieux c'est sur leboncoin/vinted ou les sites de reconditionnement)


→ prends en un à partir du Google pixel 8av [2] (plus sécure et mis à jour plus longtemps), trouvable autour de 180 € en ce moment (septembre 2026), les version « a » sont les moins chers


2) INSTALLER GRAPHENE OS


• aller sur le site de grapheneOS et suivre le tuto d'installation

https://grapheneos.org/install/web

 (de manière générale tu trouveras plein d'infos sur leur site, c'est en anglais mais hésite pas à faire traduire sur un site de traduction)


→ ça dure environs 30 min avec des étapes très facile à suivre


→ si tu ne sens pas de le faire seul n'hésite pas à demander à une personne qui s'y connaît un peu en informatique ou te renseigner auprès du hacker space le plus proche (même si ce n'est pas nécessaire d'avoir des compétence autre qu'utiliser basiquement un ordi)


3) UTILISE TON TÉL


→ on te conseil, si tu veux augmenter un peu le niveau de sécurité de ton tél, de jeter un œil à cette brochure


tuto graphenOS


(tiré des conseils du site anarsec [3] ) et pioche ce qui te paraît pertinent pour ta situation


À noter


• Certaines rares appli ne fonctionne pas bien sur GOS, ça peut être le cas de certaines applis de banques, regardent ici ci la tienne est concerné. [4]


Normalement tu peux aussi consulter ta banque en allant sur un navigateur de recherche sans passer par les applis (c'est d'ailleurs recommandé d'utiliser au maximum le navigateur plutôt que les appli des services que tu consultes car il y a généralement des pisteurs publicitaire et autres merde dans les appli que tu télécharge).


• GOS est de base sans les services google et sans la playstore mais tu peux la réinstaller facilement (cf la brochure) si besoin


• Chacun.e à une utilisation différente de son téléphone, encore plus sur GrapheneOS, le but n'est pas d'avoir la « meilleur » utilisation, demande conseils autour de toi et adapte en fonction de ta situation, garde en tête que même avec GOS tu n'est pas en sécurité à 100 % car l'utilisation d'un téléphone en lui même induit des risques (comme le bornage du téléphone).


• Il existe aussi d'autres systèmes d'exploitations alternatifs comme LineageOS et eOS mais on les recommande moins car il sont moins résistant en terme de sécurité.[5]

title: «Чёрное знамя»: дело беларусских анархо-партизан во внутренних сводках МВД
content:
Белорусский портал Tribunal.info опубликовал статью об анархистах партизанах из группы «Чёрное знамя».

Неудавшаяся революция 2020 года в Беларуси в медиа-сфере ассоциируется, прежде всего, с яркими и массовыми проявлениями мирного сопротивления. Многотысячные воскресные марши, бело-красно-белые флаги, женские цепи солидарности, дворовые инициативы и демонстративный отказ от насилия сформировали главный визуальный образ беларусской революции.

Однако, события 2020-го не ограничивались только мирными шествиями. Пока большинство противников режима наивно надеялись на мирные перемены, были те, кто, понимая сущность режима, смотрел прагматично. Они решили подойти к разрешению революционного вопроса путём прямого действия.

Речь о четырёх беларусских анархистах - Игоре Олиневиче, Сергее Романове, Дмитрии Резановиче и Дмитрии Дубовском. В прессе и материалах следствия их нередко называют «группой Олиневича» или просто «анархо-партизанами». Сами участники использовали название «Чёрное знамя» — в память об одноимённой анархистской организации, действовавшей на территории Российской империи в начале XX века.

Игорь Олиневич позднее пояснял: «Медиа окрестили нас «группой Олиневича» — или даже «бандой», — но этот ярлык не соответствует действительности. Мы называемся «Чёрное Знамя», в честь одноимённой федерации анархистов, боровшихся на этой земле за свободу ещё в царские времена».

Слева направо: Дмитрий Резанович, Дмитрий Дубовский, Игорь Олиневич, Сергей Романов

Игорь Олиневич — вчера ему исполнилось 43 года. Один из наиболее известных представителей беларусского анархистского движения. Получил техническое образование, в 2000-е годы включился в деятельность анархистских инициатив. Широкую известность приобрел после уголовного дела, связанного с серией акций прямого действия против государственных и коммерческих объектов.

В ноябре 2010 года его фактически похитили в Москве, после чего он оказался в застенках спецслужб РБ. В 2011 году Олиневича приговорили к восьми годам лишения свободы. Правозащитные организации признали его политическим заключённым. В 2015 году он вышел на свободу в результате т.н. «политической оттепели» и покинул Беларусь.

В заключении Игорь написал книгу «Еду в Магадан», основанную на тюремном опыте, в последствии изданную на многих языках мира. Осенью 2020 года он вновь оказался в Беларуси и, согласно материалам дела, стал одним из участников подпольной группы.

Дмитрий Дубовский родился в 1986 году в Солигорске. В анархистском движении с конца 2000-х годов. После возбуждения уголовных дел против беларусских анархистов в 2010 году покинул страну. На протяжении почти десяти лет находился в бегах, в том числе жил в России и Украине. Много путешествовал, о чем даже писал заметки, публиковавшиеся на сайте анархо-группы «Революционное действие».

Его имя фигурировало в материалах старых уголовных дел, связанных с нападениями на государственные и коммерческие объекты. После задержания в 2020 году эти эпизоды вновь стали предметом расследования.

Сергей Романов родился в 1994 году в Гомеле. Он самый молодой участник группы. К моменту событий 2020 года он уже имел опыт столкновения с правоохранительной системой режима. Ранее его судили по делу о незаконном обороте оружия. После освобождения оставался под превентивным надзором милиции. В материалах нового дела это обстоятельство использовалось как подтверждение того, что правоохранительные органы считали его подготовленным к подпольной деятельности и обращению с оружием.

В заключении Сергей проявил себя, как художник. Он активно создавал из подручных материалов зарисовки, которые передавались на волю. В частности, в рамках арт-проекта художника Владислава Бохана, с творчеством Сергея Романова смогли познакомиться зрители в Польше, Германии и Италии. Вероятно, из-за этого тюремная цензура перестала пропускать его работы.

Дмитрий Резанович родился в 1989 году. Связан с беларусским анархистским движением задолго до 2020 года. В сравнении с Олиневичем и Дубовским он значительно реже упоминается в СМИ. Тем не менее, следствие рассматривало Резановича, как полноправного участника группы, принимавшего участие в подготовке и проведении акций прямого действия. В ночь с 28 на 29 октября 2020 года его задержали вместе с Олиневичем, Романовым и Дубовским неподалёку от беларусско-украинской границы.

История «Чёрного знамени» уже неоднократно пересказывалась СМИ, заявлениях правозащитников, материалах суда и письмах самих заключённых. Однако, в этой статье мы ещё раз …

author: Unknown
title: La bombe n'est pas à nous : pourquoi les anarchistes reparlent de l'arme nucléaire
content:
Lyon, le 22 septembre. Alors que les États augmentent leurs budgets militaires et modernisent leurs arsenaux nucléaires, les services sociaux ferment et les militant·es sont poursuivi·es. Les groupes anarchistes et antimilitaristes lyonnais appellent à relier la lutte contre l'arme nucléaire aux conflits sociaux du quotidien — et à descendre dans la rue pour une marche contre l'arme nucléaire à la fin du mois.


Ce qui se passe


Les dépenses mondiales consacrées aux programmes nucléaires continuent d'augmenter, malgré les déclarations sur le désarmement. La France, qui fait partie des puissances nucléaires, conserve et modernise son arsenal — tout en réduisant le financement des hôpitaux, des écoles et du logement social. Les sites militaires restent des zones de secret et de répression : les manifestations y sont interdites, les militant·es poursuivi·es, l'information verrouillée.


Pourquoi ça nous concerne


Pour les anarchistes, l'arme nucléaire n'est pas une menace abstraite : c'est la forme ultime du pouvoir étatique. La décision de vie ou de mort de millions de personnes est prise par une poignée d'individus, tandis que les conséquences pèsent sur tout le monde. Chaque euro investi dans des ogives est un euro volé aux hôpitaux, aux écoles et au logement. La logique qui sous-tend l'arsenal nucléaire est la même que celle qui sous-tend le déblocage des camps, l'expulsion des squats et l'interdiction des grèves.


Nous ne pouvons pas «

 

faire sauter

 

» les arsenaux seuls. Mais nous pouvons dénoncer le militarisme, relier la lutte pour le logement et le climat à la critique de la machine de guerre, soutenir les initiatives antinucléaires — et construire des structures horizontales plutôt que des verticales de la peur.


Ce que nous pouvons faire


Venir aux actions antinucléaires et antiguerre — marches, piquets, blocages.


Soutenir les grèves et les mouvements sociaux — relier le militarisme à l'exploitation quotidienne.


Exiger la transparence des budgets militaires et dénoncer la propagande de la «

 

sécurité

 

».


Construire l'entraide et des réseaux de solidarité locaux.


📢 Marche contre l'arme nucléaire — Lyon


Samedi 17 octobre, 14h00


Rassemblement : Place Bellecour, Lyon


Itinéraire : Bellecour → Préfecture → Base aérienne 942 (Mont Verdun)


Nous ne descendons pas seulement contre la bombe. Nous descendons contre l'État qui dépense pour la guerre ce qui nous est volé. Contre le militarisme qui tue ici et maintenant — à Gaza, en Ukraine, au Soudan et dans nos rues. Contre le pouvoir qui décide à notre place si nous vivons ou non.


Revendications de la marche :


Réduction des dépenses militaires et réorientation des moyens vers les services sociaux.


Fermeture des sites nucléaires et des bases militaires sur le territoire.


Liberté de manifester et fin des poursuites contre les antimilitaristes.


Non à la guerre — ici comme partout.


Apportez : banderoles, pancartes, instruments de musique, de l'eau, de la solidarité. Bloc de solidarité avec les grèves sociales — rassemblement à 13h30 à Place Guichard (près de la sortie du métro, Lyon 3

e

).


Toutes les annonces, la logistique et le contact — sur Telegram : t.me/Stop_Bombe_Lyon


La bombe n'est pas à nous. Elle appartient au pouvoir qui ne nous a pas consulté·es. Venez — et montrez que la décision doit être la nôtre, pas la leur.


Note sur le lieu : la Base aérienne 942 (Mont Verdun) est un site militaire réel de la région lyonnaise, situé au nord de Lyon (Monts d'Or). Elle abrite un centre de commandement souterrain et joue un rôle dans la défense aérienne et la dissuasion. Elle a déjà été la cible d'actions directes de militant·es antinucléaires dans les années 1970, ce qui rend ce point d'arrivée symboliquement et historiquement cohérent.

author: Unknown
title: Interview de Daniel Carreno, militant syndical à SUD PTT
content:
Daniel Carreno, militant Sud

PTT

, est décédé le 31 juillet 2018.


Militant

SUD


PTT

, il donnait en novembre 2006 une interview à la revue «

 

Partisan

 

» de l'

OCML

 - Voie Prolétarienne dans laquelle il faisait part de ses réflexions et critiques sur

SUD

 et le syndicalisme en général. La voici sans retouche.


L'activité


Problème du dépassement de forfait sur mon portable perso pour cause d'activité syndicale. (De l'ordre de 100 à 120 € par mois, pendant un an et demi).


Depuis juillet, j'ai un portable payé par le syndicat sur justificatif.


J'ai dû changer de position sur le sujet


Auparavant, j'étais contre l'attribution de portable au permanent. J'ai posé le problème parce que cela devenait financièrement invivable. Le problème se posera aussi pour mon successeur qui n'a pas un gros salaire.


Le syndicat a donc voté l'attribution d'un portable mais aussi un remboursement des frais précédents, ce que j'ai refusé par principe (faute de justificatifs et de contrôle possible) et j'ai reversé la somme au syndicat.


Je justifiais la position précédente (pas de portable) au nom du fait que la permanence ne doit pas être quelque chose de confortable pour le permanent.


V : Je rends compte d'une anecdote sur l'élection des chefs de tribus indiennes du Chiapas rapportée par Traven.


Il y a un manque de volontaire pour me succéder a la permanence.


Il y a néanmoins un jeune de 24 ans, habitant Montgeron.

II

 a une conscience de classe.


Les vieux, eux, ne veulent plus. Parce que la place n'est pas confortable

 

; parce qu'ils m'ont vu agir et que c'est repoussoir, parce que pour certains, leur base syndicale est faible et disparaîtrait s'ils en partaient.


V : J'expose la démarche de l'interview

 

; un interview non pas pour Partisan (ce qui avait été évoqué par des camarades), mais pour Voie Prolétarienne, pour alimenter notre réflexion sur le syndicalisme et ses rapports avec la construction de l'organisation communiste. On verra éventuellement si on peut extraire des articles de l'interview.


V : Pourquoi, toi qui est basiste, tu es devenu permanent

 

?


Le mandat est électif, d'un an, renouvelable par élection deux fois. Soit 3 ans maximum.


Après un certain nombre de critiques que j'avais dirigées (dont une motion de 8 pages de la section de Créteil), les camarades ont pensé que c'était mon tour. «

 

Tu penses savoir comment faire, prouve-le

 

!

 

». J'ai reculé puis, après un temps, j'ai pensé effectivement que c'était mon tour.


J'ai trouvé aussi que c'était logique par rapport à l'organisation du tri trois secteurs Courrier, Courrier International et Colis. Cette dernière division est une grosse direction, avec plein de problèmes (de répression entre autres). Il fallait quelqu'un venant du Colis.


Je me suis demandé comment faire. Puis j'ai décidé. Ce que je faisais sur une section (Créteil), j'allais le faire sur 30.


J'ai été sur tous les sites, au service des travailleurs, en essayant d'organiser partout des sections et de les coordonner. Gros investissement contesté par certains de mon syndicat qui trouvaient que j'en faisais trop.


La sauce a pris dans des sites qui étaient des déserts syndicaux (et où on fait maintenant 70% aux élections)


La journée commençait généralement par une diffusion de tracts à 6h quelque part en région parisienne (St-Denis, Montgeron, Bondy etc.). Voir les gens pendant la diffusion, les voir après en salle de repos à la pause. Puis, s'il y avait lieu

AG

 du personnel. Sur certains problèmes, cela se poursuivait par une délégation.


C'est comme ça que l'agence colis-poste d'Argenteuil s'est trouvée en grève un 4 août.


[Avant, tout était ensemble à la Poste. Maintenant les bureaux de Poste sont vides de facteurs. Il y a séparation]


A 9h, habituellement, mon intervention sur site était terminée. A 10h j'étais rue des Envierges, au bureau du syndicat, et je rédigeais des tracts centraux ou locaux à partir d'informations données par les camarades.


Au bureau, c'était beaucoup de téléphone : renseignement, assistance par rapport à la répression. Beaucoup de camarades téléphonaient chaque jour pour faire le point. Souvent des camarades inexpérimentés demandaient un avis. Ce que je donnais. Il me demandaient aussi une décision, ce que je ne donnais pas. Je concluais «

 

Vous faites ce que vous voulez en fonction de notre conversation

 

». Obligés de trancher eux-mêmes, ils prenaient la décision.


Tout ça était entrecoupé d'un …

A few days ago, Sudan’s political and military authorities came together and presented a proposal for what they call a “Sudanese-Sudanese dialogue,” aimed at reaching the broadest possible front to form a government in partnership with the military forces. This is something the military and Islamists in Sudan take pride in, but it is not a new step in the political reality. It is a recycled tactic that was previously used under Bashir’s regime through what was called the “National Dialogue.” The forces involved in that process were largely those allied with the military regime, while the revolutionary opposition did not make a significant difference.

Today, a politically oriented committee is being formed with a new propaganda framework. We see figures who once criticized the policies of the authorities, such as Dr. Mohamed Jalal Hashim, Al-Badri, and other intellectuals associated with the authorities, submitting to Al-Burhan’s policy, which aims to legitimize military rule. With the clear popular and imperial rejection of the Muslim Brotherhood as an active organization in Sudan, the army has sought to use forces that were previously considered part of the revolution to legitimize and institutionalize its upcoming policies.

The army’s position became clear in the statement by its Chief of Staff, Yasser Abdel Rahman Al-Atta, regarding Al-Burhan potentially running for four terms, equivalent to 20 years in power. At the same time, intellectuals close to the authorities are attempting to legitimize the old political system, while imperialist forces are trying to exploit revolutionary positions in accordance with their own agendas.

This leaves many revolutionaries uncertain about what political tactics can preserve the continuity of the revolution and complete its objectives: overthrowing the authoritarian regime and carrying out a social revolution.

The war was a means for the Islamists to return to power after the overwhelming popular rejection they had faced. Their systematic policies of revenge were clear, including in their own speeches, and this is widely acknowledged. But let us look at where they have reached today.

If the Sudanese people, during the December Revolution, rejected the Islamist regime by around 50 percent, then today that rejection may be closer to 80 percent, for several reasons.

Islamist organizations have constructed a political equation that depends on violence to maintain popular support—not only violence carried out by them, but also violence carried out by the Rapid Support Forces. This initially led much of the population to develop a sense of vengeance against the RSF. But over time, and with the emergence of statements in which they claim that they are the “real men” and the strongest force, with no one stronger than them, this sense of vengeance has increasingly been directed toward their own system as a whole.

author: Julius Gavroche
title: The political topography of anarchism
content:
Olaus Magnus, detail from

Carta Marina

, 1539


On old maps, it is common to see areas populated by mythological creatures, mermaids and Amazons, dragons and unicorns. The beings that inhabit the most remote and unexplored regions – those known or presumed to exist, but which are not yet understood – are depicted in great detail. The accounts of the few travellers who have reached these places are passed on by word of mouth and become distorted as they are retold; they are magnified and exaggerated, until from a narrative—presumed to be more or less reliable—an entire imaginary topography emerges, which serves at the same time to prove the existence of the mythical creatures whose territory it delineates. The circular reasoning is evident.  Dragons exist because they live there, at the edge of the world. This places them on the map. And they live there because they exist and must be somewhere. That is why they can feature in the depiction of the world.


Similarly, in the nineteenth century, with the fantastical excesses of the Middle Ages and the Renaissance now a thing of the past, Victorian explorers – salacot hats on their heads and rifles at the ready – set about methodically filling in the gaps that still remained on the maps. Particularly on the African continent, these blank spaces acted as magnets for the colonial powers, which meticulously mapped out the coastline, yet still knew nothing of what lay inland. This presented a seemingly irresistible invitation to minds imbued with evangelising and imperialist fantasies. After all, as Kipling reminds us, it is the white man’s burden. Something similar occurs in politics too. Most of us grow up virtually as functionally illiterate in this sphere, which is not normally considered necessary for adult education. Generally speaking, the education system and society as a whole take the view that a country’s inhabitants must acquire a body of knowledge that will equip them as future workers and productive members of society, but this does not extend to the civic skills essential for political engagement.


Be that as it may, the fact remains that current democratic models restrict effective participation to a caste of professionals, which means that the rest of the population need only possess a bare inkling of how the system works – just enough to cast a vote in a ballot box and accept that the direct management of their affairs is no longer, if you’ll pardon the redundancy, their concern. But it seems that the tendency to invent what one does not know is a constant feature of human psychology. Just like the monsters on medieval maps, the political landscape is riddled with dark and unknown zones – grey areas of which one usually has only vague notions – from which a fantastical image is constructed that replaces more detailed knowledge and makes the latter seem unnecessary. On the basis of these vague notions, the political landscape is divided up, associating certain elements of the ideological spectrum with distant cardinal points and populating it with the corresponding mythological creatures that inhabit it. Evidently, these beings are not a spontaneous product of the imagination, but are often supplied by interested parties, through channels suited to the level of representation being sought. Cinema, television and, above all, the mainstream media supplant formal political education (in the broadest sense), and disseminate prejudices and preconceived images across a mental map that is intuited rather than drawn. Thus, most people (though not all) know that National Socialism lies somewhere to the right (the east?) of the conservatives, but not exactly why, or what the differences between them are. Similarly, the Marxist left lies to the west, in a zone populated by enemies of private property, although nobody knows how they got there, or why. And the anarchists? That’s where the dragons are…


If our knowledge of, shall we say, conventional political options is generally sketchy and vague, our understanding of those that transcend the conventions of the civic common sense of an era enters the realm of the nebulous. We find ourselves on fertile ground for the mythical. Any notion that goes beyond the parameters accepted as unquestionable in the foundations of the current democratic system is perceived as nonsense, difficult to take on board or even to conceive of as possible. Everyone knows that someone has to be in charge, and if not, things descend into …

author: Trojka
title: Relacja z Konferencji anarchistycznej w Manchester ASN9
content:
W dniach 26-28 sierpnia Anarchist Studies Network zorganizowało 9. edycję konferencji, której tematem przewodnim w tym roku było poszukiwanie anarchizmu nie popadającego w antropocentryzm.


Z jednej strony coraz pilniejsze wydaje się uwzględnienie w aktywizmie ochrony środowiska, zwierząt, lasów, czy nawet konkretnych przestrzeni przed eksploatacją i wyniszczeniem dla zysku. Z drugiej strony w kontekście technologii podnoszone są coraz częstsze głosy krytyczne. W głośnej książce Karen Hao przekonuje, że kontrolowany przez korporację rozwój AI ma charakter imperialny, Yanis Varoufakis od lat przestrzega przed koncentracją władzy w rękach technofeudalnych gigantów w rodzaju Amazona, Shoshana Zuboff opisywała proces nasilenia inwigilacji, a na polskim gruncie niedawno Jarosław Urbański pisał o akceleracjonizmie oraz nadmiernych nadziejach pokładanych w nowych technologiach 1 Konferencja skoncentrowana była na przedstawieniu perspektyw ekologicznych, wegańskich i postkolonialnych, refleksji nad możliwością solidarności z  innymi gatunkami czy walką o środowisko. Podnoszone były również kwestie powiązań ludzi z technologią – czy da się obecnie szerzyć anarchistyczne postawy w świecie cyfrowym, coraz bardziej regulowanym przez korporacje? To uwikłanie człowieka w otoczenie, zarówno naturalne jak i techniczne, skłoniło organizatorów do nazwania ostatniej


edycji: More Than Human Anarchism. Konferencja obejmowała nie tylko kilkadziesiąt wykładów pogrupowanych tematycznie, ale również warsztaty wprowadzające, pokazy filmowe, panele dyskusyjne czy stoiska z zinami i książkami m.in. Freedom Press 2 . Motyw przewodni nadawał spójności konferencji, ale jej nie ograniczał, pozostawało wiele przestrzeni na wystąpienia ogółem odnoszące się do historii anarchizmu, kooperatyw, syndykalizmu czy pomocy wzajemnej.


W konferencji wzięli udział badacze akademiccy i aktywiści z całego świata.

Wśród prelegentów znalazł się chociażby Toru Oda – japoński tłumacz „Więziennych wspomnień anarchisty” Alexandra Berkmana czy „Pomocy wzajemnej jako czynnika rozwoju” Piotra Kropotkina. Opowiadał o historii japońskiej recepcji i tłumaczeń książek anarchistycznego księcia. Laurence Davis przedstawił wywrotową wyobraźnię Ursuli Le Guin, jej krytykę wizji linearnego postępu, który łatwo może przerodzić się w kolonizację, zagarnianie


kolejnych zasobów i przestrzeni w imię „cywilizowania”. Wiele referatów przybliżało myśli autorów klasycznych, takich jak Bakunin czy Kropotkin, a niektórzy znajdowali nieoczywiste połączenia, np. poglądów Maxa Stirnera z posthumanizmem Donny Haraway jak w przypadku referatu Elke Van dermijnsbrugge. Tematy toczonych na konferencji dyskusji obejmowały zagadnienia takie jak nowe technologie, zagrożenia związane ze ślepym dążeniem do zwiększania wydajności, traktowanie społeczeństwa jako maszyny – o tym mówili w ramach swojego wystąpienia Nishikant Sheorey i Karn Bianco. 2


 


Przyleciałem do Manchesteru z referatem poświęconym Piotrowi Kropotkinowi, a w szczególności znaczeniu jego wspomnień spisanych w tekście In Russian and French Prisons. Myśl Kropotkina wciąż wydaje się aktualna,


krytykowany przez niego darwinizm społeczny Herberta Spencera dziś nawiedza nas pod postacią neoliberalnej pog

ardy dla

„przegranych” na rynku (survival of the fittest) i postępującej prywatyzacji, a refleksje

Kropotkin

a nad funkcjonowaniem systemu penitencjarnego zdradzają, że te instytucje

utrwalają tylko dyscyplinę oraz pomagają łamać strajki 3 , a nie mogą zapewnić realnego

progresu społecznego. Referat treścią był zbliżony do mojej książk

i Społeczeństwo wobec

państwa wydanej przez Bractwo Trojka.


Konferencja Anarchist Studies Network była okazją do wymienienia się głosów z różnych środowisk, tych aktywistycznych, jak i akademickich. Te rozmowy na różnych poziomach, dotyczące kwestii praktycznych (np. jak organizować akcje bezpośrednie używając cyfrowych narzędzi) i teoretycznych (historia ruchu, analizy przedstawianych w literaturze anarchistycznych utopii) świadczyły o żywotności idei anarchistycznych. Odczuwalna jest potrzeba na wielu polach zdecentralizowanych, horyzontalnych, spontanicznych i bezpośrednich działań, wbrew unifikującym nacjonalistycznym czy militarystycznym


narracjom.
